_why: ADR 0136's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The finding: `build_report` rendered a Result section and the only
production caller never passed it a simulation, so the one command whose
purpose is 'run the simulation and show where the numbers came from' did
the second half only. The unit test passed throughout by building its
own Trajectory -- a test that constructs its own input cannot verify how
The find strings are the CURRENT lines, not the ones the ADR was written
against: ADR 0141 and 0142 have edited this file since. A set file is a
claim about the code as it stands, so re-deriving it after later work is
the point of having one -- a set that only ever matched the tree on the
day it was written would rot into an INDETERMINATE nobody investigates.
The fourth mutation in the ADR's table -- reading the payload instead of
the derived inputs for the ensemble -- SURVIVED on its first run and is
recorded there as a survivor. It is not in this set because the test
that closes it was added in the same pass and the mutation now fails;
keeping it would restate a caught mutation as if it had always been one.

mutations.description: refusals established by the caller are dropped
mutations._note: 'The model was not run, and here is what was missing' is a refusal build_report cannot see for itself. Dropping it leaves a document that is silent about its own biggest gap.
